paper.title: A Causal Bandit Approach to Learning Good Atomic Interventions in Presence of Unobserved Confounders

settings.name_in_paper: Causal bandits, simple regret, semi-Markovian causal graph with atomic interventions and unobserved confounders
unmapped: Arms are 2N atomic interventions do(X_i=x), x in {0,1}, plus an observational arm do()
After each pull the learner observes the values of all observable nodes of the causal Bayesian network (causal side information), not only the reward
The learner knows the causal graph (ADMG) but not the distribution
Intervenable nodes are Bernoulli given parents; graph is semi-Markovian with identifiable hidden confounders (no bi-directed path from X to a child of X)
settings.definition_quote:
A causal bandit algorithm receives as input a CBN $\mathcal{C} = (\mathcal{G}, .)$, the associated set of intervenable nodes $\mathbf{X} \subseteq \mathbf{V}$ and the designated reward node $Y\in \mathbf{V}$; in particular the algorithm only receives as input the causal graph $\mathcal{G}$, but the $\mathbb{P}$ associated with $\mathcal{C}$ is unknown to the algorithm. 
 We assume there are $N$ intervenable nodes $\mathbf{X} = \{X_1, \ldots, X_N\}$, and there are $2N$ interventions denoted $a_{i,x} = do(X_i =x)$ for $i\in [N]$ and $x\in \{0,1\}$. The empty intervention $do()$ is denoted as $a_0$. These $2N+1$ interventions constitute the arms $\mathcal{A}= \{a_{i,x} \mid i \in [N], x\in \{0,1\}\} \cup \{a_0\}$ of the bandit instance.

settings.name_in_paper: Causal bandits, simple regret, fully observable n-ary tree / specific causal graphs (lower bound)
unmapped: Arms are atomic interventions plus the observational arm; all nodes observed after each pull
The learner knows the causal graph; all nodes observable
settings.definition_quote: Each graph in T is an n-ary tree, where each node can have 2 to n children. Additionally, all the leaves in the graph are connected to the outcome node Y ... We also assume that all the nodes of a graph in T is observable

settings.name_in_paper: Causal bandits, cumulative regret, general fully observable causal graph with atomic interventions
unmapped: Arms are atomic interventions plus the observational arm; all nodes observed after each pull (observational samples used via backdoor adjustment)
The learner knows the causal graph; all nodes observable
Positivity: P(X_i=x, Pa(X_i)=z) > 0 for all i, x, z
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we propose \CRM, an algorithm to minimize the cumulative regret for a CBN $\mathcal{C} = (\mathcal{G},.)$, where $\mathcal{G}$ is a general causal graph with atomic interventions. Though unlike in \SRM, here we assume all nodes in $\mathcal{G}$ are observable. We also assume $\mathbb{P}(X_i = x, \mathbf{Pa}(X_i) = \mathbf{z}) > 0$ for all $i,x$ and $\mathbf{z}$.

symbols.m_C: m(C) = min{tau : |{i : q_i^{k_i} < 1/tau}| <= tau}, instance-dependent number of poorly estimated interventions

conditions: identifiability: no bi-directed path from an intervenable node X to a child of X
tuning: T/2 observational pulls then uniform interventions on estimated poorly-covered arms

source.label: theorem: UB-SR
source.quote: The expected simple regret of \SRM\ at the end of $T$ rounds is $r_{\SRM}(T) = O\bigg(\sqrt{\frac{m(\mathcal{C})}{T}\log \frac{NT}{m(\mathcal{C})}}\bigg)$, where $\mathcal{C}$ is the input CBN.

results.notes: Hidden constant depends on graph structure (K_G exponential in k, d). Proof assumes T >= max(L1,L2). Polynomial compute claimed relative to in-degree of Y.

symbols.m_C: m(C) of the constructed CBN, equal to any chosen M <= N_int

conditions: causal graph is any n-ary tree in class T (leaves connected to Y), all nodes observable
for every positive integer M <= N there exists a distribution with m(C) = M

source.label: theorem: LB-Tree
source.quote: Corresponding to every causal graph $\mathcal{G} \in \mathsf{T}$, with $N$ intervenable nodes and a positive integer $M \leq N$, there exists a probability measure $\mathbb{P}$ and CBN $\mathcal{C} = (\mathcal{G}, \mathbb{P})$ such that $m(\mathcal{C}) = M$ and the expected simple regret of any causal bandit algorithm \texttt{ALG} is $r_{\texttt{ALG}}(T) = \Omega\big(\sqrt{m(\mathcal{C})/T} \big)$.

conditions: specific fully observable causal graph with N >= 3 intervenable nodes (X_N parent of all others, all connected to Y)
holds for any valid q vector

source.label: theorem: LB-given-q
source.quote: There exists a fully observable causal graph $\mathcal{G}$ with $N \geq 3$ nodes such that given a valid $\mathbf{q}$ corresponding to $\mathcal{G}$ there is a probability measure $\mathbb{P}$ conforming with $\mathbf{q}$ and CBN $\mathcal{C} = (\mathcal{G},\mathbb{P})$ for which expected simple regret of any causal bandit algorithm $\Omega\big(\sqrt{m(\mathcal{C})/T} \big)$.

results.notes: Shows the q-dependence of m is optimal for this graph.

bound.regime: observational arm a_0 is optimal; T sufficiently large

conditions: optimal arm is the observational arm a_0
tuning: beta updated as min{2 sqrt(2)/(mu_hat* - mu_hat_0), sqrt(log t)}

source.label: theorem: UB-CRM
source.quote: If $a* = a_0$ then at the end of $T$ rounds the expected cumulative regret is $O(1)$

results.notes: Proof gives sum_{Delta_a>0} Delta_a pi^2/3 for T large enough (instance-dependent constant).

bound.regime: observational arm not optimal; T >= max(L, exp(50/Delta_0^2))

symbols.Delta_0: gap of the observational arm a_0
symbols.p_i: p_{i,x} = min_z P(X_i=x, Pa(X_i)=z) for interventional arm (i,x)
symbols.eta_i: eta_T^{i,x} = max{0, 1 - Z_i T^{-p_{i,x}^2/4}}, Z_i = domain size of Pa(X_i)

conditions: optimal arm is not the observational arm

source.label: theorem: UB-CRM
source.quote: and otherwise the expected cumulative regret is of the order $\frac{58\ln{T}}{\Delta_0} + \Delta_0 + \sum_{\Delta_{i,x}>0} \Delta_{i,x} \max \bigg(0, 1 + 8\ln{T}\bigg(\frac{1}{\Delta_{i,x}^2} - \frac{p_{i,x} \cdot \eta_T^{i,x}}{36 \Delta_0^2} \bigg) \bigg) + \sum_{\Delta_a > 0} \Delta_a \frac{\pi^2}{3}$.

results.notes: First sum ranges over interventional arms (i,x) only (excludes a_0); written with sum_subopt as approximation. Paper says 'of the order'.
